title: Optimum bound for filtered long-code instance
statement: Let $G$ be a regular unique game with a nonempty finite label set, and let a tester family satisfy the dictator-versus-no-notables conditions with parameters $\alpha$ and $\beta$ and error function $\operatorname{error}$. Choose a uniform refinement of the tester’s allowed weighted constraint experiment, and let $r,M$ be natural numbers with $0<M$ and $r\le M$, such that every tester predicate has arity at most $r$. If $0<\epsilon\le1$ and the optimum of the constraint satisfaction instance associated to $G$ is less than $\tau\epsilon^5/18$, then the optimum of the globally filtered long-code constraint satisfaction instance is at most $\alpha+\operatorname{error}(\epsilon)+\tau+r^2/M$.

A uniform refinement of the allowed weighted constraint experiment
Every tester predicate has arity at most $r$
The original game instance optimum is less than $\tau\epsilon^5/18$
caveat: The tester conditions and the construction of the globally filtered instance are bundled upstream definitions; the statement describes their mathematical roles.
